findings.title: Strategy close shuts down the shared queue pool, breaking rebalances and losing messages
findings.body: `ResultsStrategyFactory` creates one `FixedQueuePool` in its constructor and passes that same pool to every `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` created by `create_with_partitions`. On Kafka partition revocation/reassignment, Arroyo closes the previous strategy, and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`. This shuts down worker threads and queues that are owned by the long-lived factory. The next strategy created from that factory then submits to a shut-down pool: `work_queue.put()` raises `queue.ShutDown`, which is caught by the broad `except Exception` in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`, and the offset is marked complete without ever invoking `result_processor`. Messages are silently skipped and their offsets are committed. The pool lifecycle should be separated from the per-assignment strategy lifecycle.

findings.title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure and can exhaust memory
findings.body: Each queue in `FixedQueuePool` is created as `queue.Queue()` with no max size. The strategy docstring claims 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but these queues never fill up. If one group's worker is slow or processing stalls, that queue can grow without bound, consuming all available memory and allowing consumer lag to grow indefinitely. Use a bounded `Queue(maxsize=...)` and handle `QueueFull`, or otherwise bound pending work so backpressure is actually exerted on the Arroyo submit loop.

findings.title: Failed result processing still completes the offset and allows commit
findings.body: `OrderedQueueWorker.run` catches any exception from `result_processor`, logs it, and then the `finally` block always calls `offset_tracker.complete_offset`. This means an unexpected failure that escapes `ResultProcessor.__call__` is treated as successfully processed; the commit loop later commits past it. The message is never retried and is not routed to a DLQ. The worker should only complete the offset when processing succeeds, or explicitly mark poison messages for the configured DLQ path.

findings.title: Unexpected submit-time failures mark the message complete, silently skipping it
findings.body: In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`, any exception from `decoder`, `grouping_fn`, or work-item construction is caught, logged, and then the offset is both added and completed. As a result, a message that cannot be decoded or grouped due to a bug is committed and never processed instead of propagating to Arroyo's error/DLQ handling. This can cause silent loss of subscription results. Only the explicit `decoder` returning `None` case should be skipped; unexpected exceptions should not complete the offset.

findings.title: Invalid or zero max_workers silently creates 20 queues
findings.body: `num_queues=max_workers or 20` means `0`, negative values, and other falsy values all become 20 worker threads. Passing `--max-workers 0` or a negative value unexpectedly starts 20 threads instead of being rejected. `max_workers` should be explicitly validated as a positive integer when `mode` is `thread-queue-parallel`.
